features.feature_value: Compared how egregious both sides were to decide keep vs remove.
features.evidence_span: looking at both statements to see how egregious they were on both sides
features.rationale: The participant explicitly describes using a bilateral comparison of severity across the pair.

features.feature_value: Used a boundary between free speech and harassment/violent rhetoric.
features.evidence_span: line between free speech and what I would consider genuine harassment or violent rhetoric
features.rationale: They state a specific decision rule: allow speech unless it crosses into harassment/violence.

features.feature_value: Removed comments perceived as hostile/insulting; emphasized dialogue and safety for minors.
features.evidence_span: stick to comments where each side was trying to make a point that might actually start a dialogue
features.rationale: They connect keep/remove to whether the tone enables dialogue and whether content is safe for minors.

features.feature_value: Removal depended on how vile the comments were.
features.evidence_span: depended on how vile the comments were
features.rationale: A clear intensity threshold is described as guiding the decision.

features.feature_value: Chose not to allow the opposing content if it was very inaccurate.
features.evidence_span: If the opposition was very inaccurate, I chose not to allow it through.
features.rationale: They identify factual accuracy of the opposing side as a decisive cue in the pair comparison.

features.feature_value: Relied on a free-speech principle even when disagreeing with the content.
features.evidence_span: I believe in free speech.  I didn't agree with most of what was written
features.rationale: They justify their decision with an overriding norm rather than content-specific disapproval.

features.feature_value: Considered mutual respect, whether intent mattered vs venting, and how thought-provoking the ideas were.
features.evidence_span: Mutual respect. Was intent more important than just venting? How thought-provoking were the ideas
features.rationale: They describe multiple evaluative criteria focused on intent, respect, and idea value.

features.feature_value: Wanted to shut down offensive/permanent hateful speech to enable more positive communication.
features.evidence_span: facilitate more positive communication rather than so much hateful speech
features.rationale: They explicitly mention hateful/offensive speech as the cue and a positive-communication goal as the motive.
